answer:
I can't see the repository, so this comes from memory of Dispatch's code and may not match your version.

**(a) Chat button: yes.** The subscribe button on the incident announcement message isn't tied to the project's self-join setting. As I remember it, that setting only hides or blocks the "Join" button and the participant-adding flow. Subscribing by e-mail on an open incident therefore still works for an ordinary member.

**(b) Web API: no.** The subscribe endpoint, `/incidents/{incident_id}/subscribe`, is guarded by `IncidentJoinOrSubscribePermission`. As I remember it, that class lets an ordinary member through only when the incident is open and the project allows self-join. Otherwise it requires an incident commander, a scribe, or an administrator. So in a project that blocks self-enrolment, an ordinary member gets a 403 from the API even though the chat button works.

I'm least sure of (b). If the permission class only checks visibility and ignores the project setting, the API answer would flip to yes. Reading the class's `has_required_permissions` would settle it.

FILE: src/dispatch/incident/permissions.py
CLASS: IncidentJoinOrSubscribePermission
VIA_CHAT_BUTTON: yes
VIA_API: no
